comment: Pleroma / Sandalphon seccomp profile (2026-10 §CG). defaultAction is SCMP_ACT_ALLOW (denylist style), NOT SCMP_ACT_ERRNO. A full allowlist (default-deny) profile would be the architecturally stronger design, but building one correctly requires exhaustively tracing every syscall the real python:3.11-alpine entrypoint needs for the full range of scripts this jail actually runs -- and that tracing requires running the real container, which this development environment's network allowlist blocks (container registries are unreachable here; see GRIMOIRE.md §CF). Guessing an allowlist blind risks silently breaking the sandbox's basic function in a way that would only surface later, which is the kind of unverified claim this project explicitly avoids. This denylist is therefore the honest, verifiable middle ground for now: it closes a documented, concrete set of dangerous primitives (process creation/escape, ptrace, mount/namespace manipulation, kernel module and system control, privilege-related syscalls, raw networking as defense-in-depth on top of --network none, time tampering, NUMA/keyring exotica) without risking any legitimate script execution, since none of these syscalls appear in a baseline python interpreter startup+execution trace (confirmed via strace on this host). Moving to a full allowlist is left as a documented follow-up for an environment where the real container image can actually be pulled and traced end-to-end (e.g. GitHub Actions).

syscalls.comment: Process creation / code-execution escape. The jail runs one disposable script to completion and starting a new process (fork/vfork/clone/clone3) or replacing the current image (execve/execveat) has no legitimate use here -- this is also the kernel-level backstop for the os.fork/subprocess/os.exec family that §CC and the audit-hook layers already police at the Python layer.
Process introspection / debugging. No legitimate script run in this jail needs to inspect or write into another process's memory.

Mount/filesystem-namespace manipulation. The jail's root filesystem is already --read-only; none of these operations are needed to run a script and all of them are classic container-escape primitives.
Kernel module / system-wide control. A disposable per-script container has no legitimate need to load kernel modules, reboot the host, or otherwise affect anything outside itself.

Namespace / privilege manipulation. --cap-drop=ALL (§CF) already makes most of these fail at the capability-check layer, but blocking them at the seccomp layer too is cheap defense-in-depth that fails earlier and does not depend on the capability check being correctly configured.

Raw networking, as defense-in-depth on top of --network none. AF_UNIX socket()/socketpair() do not require a network namespace and would otherwise still succeed inside this jail; blocking the whole socket-family syscall surface closes that gap rather than relying solely on there being no route.
Host clock/time tampering. No legitimate script run in this jail needs to change the system clock.
NUMA memory-policy manipulation and the kernel keyring. Historically exploit-prone, never needed by an ordinary disposable script.
Miscellaneous legacy syscalls with no legitimate use here.
